extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (research mathematicians / computational algebraists) who need to compute Hilbert series, noncommutative Hilbert series, Ore-localizations and manipulate noncommutative fractions.
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for several SINGULAR libraries (multigrading/hilbert-series utilities, ncHilb, ncfrac, ncloc) describing procedure usage, input formats, return values and examples for computing (multi-)graded Hilbert series, noncommutative Hilbert series, colon computations, nc fractions and localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbertSeries / hilb usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure (hilb/std/hilbertSeries) returns a ring containing polynomials named 'numerator1'/'numerator2' and 'denominator1'/'denominator2' representing (multi-)graded Hilbert series for the current ideal/module. The s_i variables in that ring are defined as the inverse of the t_i variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage: def h = hilbertSeries(I); setring h; then call numerator1; denominator1; to inspect the first Hilbert series numerator and denominator. Example outputs in the manual show explicit numerator/denominator polynomials (e.g. -t1^12+3*t1^8-3*t1^4+1, denominator t1^8-4*t1^6+...). Use kill h when done. The proc works for ideals and modules and prints affine/projective dimension and degree when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: lll (multigrading.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure lll takes an integer matrix (or list of intvec rows) and returns an LLL-reduced integer basis/list (used in multigrading context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: intmat m[...] = ...; lll(m); returns a set of intvec rows (reduced basis). lll(list-of-intvecs) is also supported. The manual shows example inputs and the corresponding reduced rows. Use when you need a reduced integer lattice basis for multigrading computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nchilb usage (ncHilb.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: nchilb(list_of_relations, d, optional) computes graded or multigraded Hilbert series (or truncated Hilbert series) of non-commutative algebras given a list L of modules representing a two-sided Groebner basis; d is a degree bound (max total degree) for computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional third argument meanings: 1 => computation for non-finitely generated regular ideals; 2 => compute multigraded Hilbert series; tdeg (integer) => compute truncated Hilbert series up to total degree tdeg-1 (tdeg>2); string("p") => print detailed orbit and linear system info. Input format requirement: a Groebner basis of the two-sided ideal must be provided as a list of modules where each generator lists coefficient then variables (e.g. module p1=[1,y,z],[-1,z,y] for y*z - z*y). The proc prints orbit information, maximal length of words, length of orbit, linear system for orbit series, and final Hilbert series formula. Examples show many typical calls and outputs (rational series, multigraded rational expressions).

rubrics_metrics.name: rcolon (ncHilb.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: rcolon(list_of_relations, monomial_w, d) computes the right colon (or related right-colon computation) for a two-sided monomial ideal given in the special module-list form; w is a monomial (also given as a module) and d is a degree bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input format: modules where each generator represents a monomial times coefficient, first entry 1 and subsequent entries variables (e.g. module p1=[1,y,z] for y*z). The procedure returns generators (printed) of the colon ideal corresponding to w and the given monomial ideal. Example demonstrates calling rcolon(l1,w,10) and printing output.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncfrac type overview and constructors (ncfrac.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: ncfrac is a type representing a (non-commutative) fraction in an Ore localization; an ncfrac has members polys lnum, lden, rnum, rden and ncloc loc. Several constructors are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations: string(ncfrac), print(ncfrac), status(ncfrac), test(ncfrac). Constructors: ncfrac = int/number/poly creates fraction with left/right denominators 1; ncfrac = vector sets lden,lnum,rnum,rden = v[1..4] (localization may be unspecified => invalid fraction); ncfrac = list tries to create fraction from L[1] and if L[2] is ncloc it sets localization. Care: without specifying localization, constructing from a vector may produce an invalid fraction. The manual lists infix operations (==, !=, +, -, *, /) and mixing with ints/numbers/polys.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasLeftDenom(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks whether an ncfrac has a left representation (i.e., a left denominator is known/existent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hasLeftDenom(ncfrac) returns int 1 if a left representation exists, 0 otherwise. Example in manual demonstrates creating ncfrac with loc and checking hasLeftDenom returns 0 or 1 depending on representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: hasRightDenom(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks whether an ncfrac has a right representation (i.e., a right denominator is known/existent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hasRightDenom(ncfrac) returns int 1 if a right representation exists, 0 otherwise. Example shows constructing fractions and checking result.

rubrics_metrics.name: isZeroNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether an ncfrac is the zero fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isZeroNcfrac(ncfrac) returns 1 if zero, 0 otherwise. Examples show constructing a fraction with left numerator y^2+7*y+1 and others, verifying outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: isOneNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether an ncfrac equals one in the localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isOneNcfrac(ncfrac) returns 1 if fraction equals one, 0 otherwise. Examples illustrate behavior when numerator/denominator equal and after modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: zeroNcfrac(loc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the zero fraction in the given localization loc (ncloc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: zeroNcfrac(ncloc) returns an ncfrac representing zero. Example prints left and right representations (1,0) and (0,1) format indicating zero representation forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: oneNcfrac(loc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the multiplicative identity (one) fraction in the given localization loc (ncloc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: oneNcfrac(ncloc) returns an ncfrac representing one. Example prints left and right representations (1,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ensureLeftNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that an ncfrac has a left representation, computing it if not already known. Returns an ncfrac with a left representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ensureLeftNcfrac(ncfrac) computes and returns a representation that has a left representation. Examples demonstrate for monoidal, geometric, and rational localizations; printed left and right representations are shown and validated via rm.lnum*g - rm.lden*f == 0 checks. Works for typical localizations (monoidal lists, geometric ideals, intvec for rational).

rubrics_metrics.name: ensureRightNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that an ncfrac has a right representation, computing it if not already known. Returns an ncfrac with a right representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: ensureRightNcfrac(ncfrac) computes and returns representation that has a right representation. Examples similar to ensureLeftNcfrac show left/right rep after computation and validate equality f*rm.rden - g*rm.rnum == 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: negateNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the additive inverse (negative) of an ncfrac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: negateNcfrac(ncfrac) returns (-1)*frac. Example: create fraction and call negateNcfrac; then frac + negFrac yields a representation of zero. Printed left/right representations show sign change on denominators/numerators accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInvertibleNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks if an ncfrac is invertible (has a multiplicative inverse) in its localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isInvertibleNcfrac(ncfrac) returns 1 if invertible, 0 otherwise. Example shows invertible case (1) and non-invertible case (0).

rubrics_metrics.name: invertNcfrac(frac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the inverse of an ncfrac, returning an ncfrac inverse when invertible; returns the zero fraction if not invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: invertNcfrac(ncfrac) returns ncfrac inverse or zero-fraction sentinel when not invertible. Example: invertible input returns left repr (y+1,y); non-invertible returns left repr (1,0) and right repr (0,1) (= zero fraction indicator as documented).

rubrics_metrics.name: testNcfrac() and testNcfracExamples()
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal testing utilities to exercise library procedures and example suite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: testNcfrac() executes internal tests and returns nothing; testNcfracExamples() runs the example suite demonstrating all procedures in the ncfrac library. Use them to validate correct installation/behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncloc type overview and constructors (ncloc.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: ncloc is a type wrapping localization data for Ore-localizations; members include int locType and def locData. Constructors create monoidal (list/poly), geometric (ideal), or rational (intvec) localizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations supported: string(ncloc), print(ncloc), status(ncloc), test(ncloc), equality comparisons. Constructors: ncloc = list/poly (monoidal localization), ncloc = ideal (geometric localization), ncloc = intvec (rational localization). Use appropriate constructor form depending on desired localization semantics for use with ncfrac and related routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: isDenom(p, loc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether polynomial p is a valid denominator in localization loc (ncloc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isDenom(p, ncloc) returns int 1 if p is a valid denominator in loc, 0 otherwise. Examples: for monoidal loc constructed from list L, composite g (product of generators) returns 1 while g-1 returns 0; for geometric loc = ideal(x-1,y-3), g = x^2+y-3 returns 1 while (x-1)*g returns 0; for rational localization (intvec) certain polynomials are valid denominators while others are not. Use to validate denominators before constructing or manipulating ncfrac objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: testNcloc()
rubrics_metrics.description: Run internal tests for the ncloc library to validate localization routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: testNcloc() executes a series of internal testing procedures and returns nothing. Use to check that the ncloc library functionality is working as expected.
